summary: The note describes how small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are localizing their supply chains, a trend that has grown since September 2023. It argues that local sourcing improves flexibility, sustainability, resilience, community collaboration and workforce development, supported by technology and government policy. Examples include Jackson's Bakery, WeaveWorks, Cornerstone Electronics and Greenway Organics.
one_line: SMEs are localizing supply chains to gain flexibility, resilience and sustainability while strengthening local economies, aided by technology, education and government policy.
key_facts: Since September 2023, a growing trend among SMEs has been to localize their supply chains.

Jackson's Bakery, a family-owned business in Vermont, partnered with local flour mills and regional dairy farms; owner Emily Jackson said this cut logistics costs and made products resonate with customers.
WeaveWorks, a textile company led by CEO Marcus Greene, shifted to local producers in late 2023 and reduced lead times by nearly 50%.
Jameson Tech, a local software provider led by CEO Angela Morris, offers affordable, scalable inventory and analytics solutions for SMEs and reported a surge in demand from local businesses.
The annual Local Business Expo, started in 2024, brings SMEs and local suppliers together to form and strengthen partnerships.
Greenway Organics, which makes eco-friendly cleaning products, has seen substantial sales growth since it began prioritizing local ingredients in September 2023.
As of early 2024, the Future Workforce Program has helped equip students with practical supply chain knowledge through collaboration between SMEs and local colleges and trade schools.
Cornerstone Electronics sources nearly 80% of its components from within a 150-mile radius, which let it maintain production despite a surge in global shipping costs.
In early 2024 the government introduced the Local Enterprise Support Scheme (LESS), offering tax breaks and grants to incentivize SMEs to choose local suppliers.
Sunrise Textiles expanded its operations while keeping a local-centric supply chain, helped by LESS.
Global Widgets set up local supplier workshops and participatory community events to build a local supply chain ecosystem.
The Quarterly Local Business Meet-up gives SMEs a regular platform to share resources, information and insights.
Local supply chains create a ripple effect: more local employment and increased community spending that supports other local businesses.
